record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: Does there exist, for small degree d, an irreducible component of the relative Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^n_Z) over Spec(Z) that exists only in characteristic p?

evidence.quote: Problem XXI. Does there exist a component of Hilbd(A^n_Z) that lives entirely in characteristic p, for small d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{Z}})$ denote the relative Hilbert scheme parametrizing length-$d$ zero-dimensional closed subschemes of affine $n$-space over $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})$. An irreducible component $C \subseteq \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{Z}})$ is said to live entirely in characteristic $p$ (for a prime $p$) if the structural morphism $C \to \mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})$ factors through the closed point $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{F}_p) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})$; equivalently, every point of $C$ corresponds to a subscheme over a field of characteristic $p$.

Question: Do there exist a prime $p$, integers $n \geq 1$ and a small value of $d$ (say with $d$ as small as possible), and an irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{Z}})$ that lives entirely in characteristic $p$?
artifact.status_search_result: Jelisiejew (Inventiones 2020, "Pathologies on the Hilbert scheme of points") proved that for every prime $p$ there exist irreducible components of $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{Z}})$ living entirely in characteristic $p$, but only for relatively large $d$ (and large $n$). The refinement asking whether such components exist for small $d$ appears to remain open; no source establishing existence (or non-existence) for small $d$ was found.

status_evidence.title: Pathologies on the Hilbert scheme of points
status_evidence.snippet: The Hilbert scheme of points on a higher dimensional affine space ... has components lying entirely in characteristic p for all primes p.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of components in characteristic p is established, but the construction uses relatively large d, leaving the small-d case open.
